corrosion_narrative: The average mild steel corrosion rate was 0.5136 MPY against the target of within 3.0 MPY, and the average copper corrosion rate was 0.1139 MPY against the target of within 0.5 MPY. Status: Excellent. Corrosion control was Excellent because both metals remained below their target limits during the August reporting period. Both mild steel and copper corrosion increased later in the month, so the movement should continue to be compared with product residual, ORP response, and system conductivity.
corrosion_chart_comment: Corrosion remained within target, though both mild steel and copper increased later in the month.
scale_narrative: Status: Acceptable. Traced Product averaged 73.90 ppm against the 67.00-73.00 ppm Controller Setpoint control range, with 41.8% of readings within range. Traced Product remained above the configured range at the end of the month, moving from about 73.3 ppm early to 74.5 ppm later. Conductivity was also not maintained, so the Traced Product trend is related to conductivity behavior; cycles, blowdown, makeup, or dilution changes should be corrected first before assigning the issue to feed control.
scale_chart_comment: Traced Product remained high and was still not maintained at the end of the month.
microbial_narrative: FRC data was not available in the field data for this reporting period and will be checked during the upcoming service visit. ORP did not show a strong spike response pattern during the month, but biocide relay activity was present, supporting an Acceptable microbial control status pending field residual confirmation. Copper corrosion remained below target, indicating no copper corrosion upset was observed during the reporting period.
orp_chart_comment: ORP response was not strong and should be verified with field FRC testing.
water_efficiency_narrative: Water efficiency was Critical. Conductivity averaged 477.35 uS/cm against the 570.00-630.00 uS/cm Controller Setpoint range, with only 10.1% of readings in range. Conductivity increased from about 381.2 uS/cm early in the month to 573.4 uS/cm later, but the monthly average remained below the configured range. Dilution, water loss, excess blowdown, or makeup changes should be reviewed.
conductivity_chart_comment: Conductivity increased but remained mostly below the controller setpoint range.
product_efficiency_narrative: Product efficiency needs attention because Traced Product averaged 73.90 ppm against the 70.00 ppm setpoint and the 67.00-73.00 ppm control range. Polymer consumption rate averaged 50.7%, indicating product residuals should be verified with phosphate and silica residuals during the next service visit. Because conductivity was also not maintained, product control should be reviewed together with cycles, blowdown, makeup, and dilution behavior before changing feed settings.
proactive_support_narrative: No service notes were recorded for the August reporting period. Recommended follow-up should focus on the unresolved health-check items: correct conductivity control by reviewing blowdown settings, cycles, makeup conditions, dilution, and possible water loss; then verify Traced Product residual response after conductivity control improves. Check FRC and dip-slide CFU during the upcoming service visit to confirm microbial control, and verify phosphate and silica residuals against the polymer consumption trend.
closing_summary: Overall August performance for Candler main showed Excellent corrosion control and Acceptable microbial control, while conductivity and Traced Product control require follow-up. The primary action is to stabilize conductivity first because the Traced Product deviation is linked with conductivity behavior. After water-side control is stabilized, product residual and polymer efficiency should be verified during the next service visit.
